explanation: Relocation is a crucial step in the linking and loading process where the linker or loader modifies the addresses within an object file to reflect their final memory locations.  This is necessary because object files are initially compiled with relative addresses, not knowing their final positions in memory.  Different architectures have varying relocation mechanisms, impacting the complexity of the process.  The relocation entry contains information the linker/loader uses to adjust addresses, ensuring the program runs correctly after being loaded into memory.
keywords: Relocation, Linker address modification, Object file relocation, Load time address fixup
